questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: Why top football players are paid so much money
How football players avoid serious head injuries
How clubs use brain science to help players decide
The long history of football as 'the beautiful game'
questions.why: Clubs are turning to neuroscience to see how players think and decide, and whether brain training helps.

options: The passion, and the players' skill and athleticism
Because everyone in his family plays it at weekends
Because the matches are short and easy to follow
Because he used to be a professional player himself
questions.why: Neil says it's the combination of passion and the skill and athleticism of the players.

questions.q: Why did Tom Cooke think something interesting was happening in players' brains?
options: Players often forget the rules during big matches
Players get tired very quickly in the second half
Players' brains are much bigger than average
Players make split-second choices under pressure
questions.why: He says they watch athletes make decisions in split instincts under the highest pressures.

questions.q: What did Japanese scientists find when they studied Neymar's brain in 2014?
options: It was far more active than other players' brains
It was much less active when he moved his ankle
It worked much better in the morning than at night
It reacted very strongly to fear and loud noise
questions.why: They found his brain was a lot less active than his peers' when he rotated his right ankle.

questions.q: What does Holly Bridge suggest the result about Neymar shows?
options: He was not really concentrating during the test
He needed much more training on his weaker foot
He is so skilled that it takes little conscious effort
His right ankle was injured at the time of the test
questions.why: She says the reduced activity reflects absolute expertise, done 'with very, very little conscious effort'.

questions.q: What does Tom Cooke do in training sessions?
options: Lets players rest their brains completely before games
Makes players watch long videos of past games
Asks players to train alone, away from the team
Overloads players with information in a safe setting
questions.why: He says they try to overwhelm them in a safe environment like training, where improvement happens.

questions.q: What does Holly Bridge say about emotions and performance?
options: Emotions affect performance, but can be controlled
Emotions have little effect on how players perform
Players should show as much emotion as possible
Only young, inexperienced players are affected
questions.why: She says performance is driven by your emotional state, 'something you can learn to control'.

questions.q: What does Niklas Häusler's company do with players?
options: Chooses which players should take the penalties
Checks their brainwaves before kicks, teaches calm
Designs new football boots using brain data
Records their heart rate during the whole match
questions.why: He measures players' brainwaves before important kicks and teaches them how to stay relaxed.
